versions.changelog:
# Changelog

## [1.18.0.0] - 2026-09-08

### Added

- Support for Jellyfin 12.0

# Changelog

## [1.17.3.0] - 2026-06-08

### Fixed

- Fix skipped import run if only Spotify-owned playlists are configured (see #86)

# Changelog

## [1.17.2.0] - 2026-06-02

### Changed

- use item field of a playlist track if the track field is not set (API parsing)

# Changelog

## [1.17.1.0] - 2026-05-27

### Fixed

- Update Jellyfin SDK to work with version 10.11.10

# Changelog

## [1.17.0.0] - 2026-02-24

### Changed

- Rework API interactions to work with the latest Spotify API changes (see #79)

# Changelog

## [1.16.0.0] - 2025-10-21

### Added

- Support for Jellyfin 10.11

# Changelog

## [1.15.1.0] - 2025-10-21

### Changed

- Replace the default URL for Spotify TOTP

# Changelog

## [1.15.0.0] - 2025-10-01

### Added

- Also ignore diacritics when using match level Ignore Punctuation + Case (or further relaxed levels)

### Changed

- Manual map interface now allows pasting in JSON (e.g. missing tracks file entries)
- Manual map entries can now be specified either be the previous information or just using the Spotify track ID / URI, similar to how playlist URIs are handled when configuring the plugin

# Changelog

## [1.14.1.0] - 2025-09-13

### Fixed

- Excessive memory use when updating the ISRC / MusicBrainz cache in some situations

# Changelog

## [1.14.0.0] - 2025-09-12

### Added

- New matching method via MusicBrainz and ISRC IDs
- The plugin settings page now contains a checkbox to activate the new MusicBrainz matching method
- Support for the import of the "Liked Songs" section from Spotify

### Changed

- The current scopes of the Spotify auth token are now displayed on the plugin settings page

overview: Cap the resolution a user may be served, measured against the media's actual height.
description:
Quality Gate lets Jellyfin administrators cap the resolution a user may be served. The cap is measured against the media's actual height, read from its video stream, so it holds whatever the file is called. Media above the cap is served as a capped transcode, or as a lower-resolution version of the same item where one exists, and requests for the original file are refused. Useful for bandwidth management and tiered access.

versions.changelog:
AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.15 — Jellyfin 12

### Changes

- Added support for Jellyfin 12.
- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.14 — Jellyfin 10.11

### Changes

- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

Release 2.0.0.13
AniLiberty STRM Performance Update

This update makes library generation and Skip Intro/Outro processing faster and lighter on Jellyfin, especially for larger libraries.

### Performance Improvements
- Faster full-catalog and Favorites library generation.
- Reduced CPU and memory usage during generation and library updates.
- Faster preparation of native Skip Intro/Outro data after Jellyfin starts or scans a library.
- Improved performance during repeated scheduled runs and when multiple library locations are configured.
- Reduced memory usage while processing artwork and plugin-managed library data.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

GitHub Release: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0.13
Full changelog: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/blob/aniLiberty-v2/CHANGELOG.md

Release 2.0.0.12
AniLiberty STRM Native Media Segments & Docker Playback Hardening

This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

GitHub Release: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0.12
Full changelog: https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin/blob/aniLiberty-v2/CHANGELOG.md

Release 2.0.0.11
AniLiberty STRM Support Trace & Docker Preflight

This update adds a safer diagnostics flow for Docker and headless Jellyfin setups: compact logs stay readable, while the Support Trace rail captures the full failure context needed for issue triage.

### Diagnostic Command Center
- Added a **Huge trace** switch for explicit support sessions.
- `Show logs` now remains the compact operational view for normal task results.
- `Show support trace` exposes the high-volume diagnostic stream only after Huge trace is enabled and the task is rerun.
- `Copy support bundle` packages sanitized configuration, compact logs, and captured support trace without exposing AniLiberty tokens.

### Full Exception Visibility
- Support trace now records full exception details, including stack traces and inner exceptions.
- Compact logs keep short, readable error summaries so normal UI logging does not turn into a wall of text.
- Verified with a read-only Docker output path: the trace captures the filesystem failure, plugin preflight stack, task failure stack, and remediation hint.

### Docker Output Flight Check
- Scheduled generation now validates that the configured output root is writable before fetching AniLiberty catalog data.
- Permission and path failures now stop early with a clear message about Docker volume mapping, host directory ownership, and PUID/PGID permissions.

This update tightens the Docker playback path for AniLiberty STRM Plugin and documents the supported container workflow: repository manifest install, container-visible output path, scheduled reconstruction, Jellyfin library scan, and proxied HLS playback.

### Docker Playback Proxy Rail
- Fixed a Docker/headless Jellyfin case where `ReverseVirtualPath` could resolve the playback proxy route as `file:///AniLibertyPlayback/hls`.
- Generated `.strm` files now keep the Playback Proxy Rail on HTTP/HTTPS instead of writing unusable `file://` proxy URLs.
- Added proxy endpoint tests that preserve valid absolute HTTP routes and normalize non-HTTP absolute routes back into Jellyfin route paths.

### Docker First Launch Flight Check
- Added a README path contract for Docker: plugin output path and Jellyfin media library path must use the same container-visible path.
- Documented a working volume pattern such as `/srv/aniliberty-strm:/media/aniliberty-strm`.

- Smoke-tested on Windows 10 Pro with Docker Desktop 4.51.0, Docker Engine 28.5.2, and Docker Compose 2.40.3.
- Confirmed Jellyfin scans generated output as a TV library, recognizes generated series and episodes, returns item-level playback info, rewrites HLS playlists through the proxy, and streams HLS segments through the plugin route.

### Not Included

- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

# AniLiberty API v1 Alignment, Better Metadata & Quieter Logs

This update improves AniLiberty authentication reliability, aligns the plugin with AniLiberty API v1 responses, and enhances generated metadata while keeping UI logs under control.

## Authentication & OTP
- Improved login and OTP endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and safer request validation.
- Updated OTP parsing to support the API v1 format (`otp.code`) and kept backward compatibility for older responses.
- OTP flow in the settings UI is simplified to **Start → Sign In** (the “Accept OTP” UI action was removed).

## Networking reliability
- Switched API calls to a reusable, DI-managed `HttpClient` (`IHttpClientFactory`) with consistent headers (User-Agent / Accept / Accept-Language).
- Added retry handling for rate limits (**HTTP 429**) and transient errors.
- Optimized HTTP reads using `ResponseHeadersRead` to reduce overhead and improve responsiveness.

## STRM generation & metadata quality
- Better year handling for AniLiberty v1 (`release.year` instead of `season.year`), including TV show year selection across grouped seasons.
- More accurate content classification:
  - Detects **MOVIE** by API `type.value` when available.
  - Routes **SPECIAL / OVA / OAD** into **Season 00** more reliably.
- Improved image handling:
  - Supports v1 image schema (`preview/thumbnail/optimized`) and prefers non-optimized URLs when possible.
  - Normalizes `.webp` URLs to `.jpg` and safely determines thumbnail file extensions even when URLs contain query parameters.
- Episode NFO improvements:
  - Writes episode titles (RU/EN when available), runtime, year, and sets `lockdata=false`.

## Logging & settings
- Added **“Enable debug logs (very noisy)”** setting:
  - When OFF: DEBUG/TRACE aren’t stored in UI logs and per-title progress logging is throttled to avoid bloating the UI log.
- UI log filtering now respects minimum log level and the debug toggle.

## Developer / maintenance
- Manual generation test is now **skipped by default** and uses environment variables (`ANI_TOKEN`, `ANI_OUTPUT_DIR`) so tokens aren’t stored in the repo.
- Internal null-safety improvements around plugin initialization.

## Not included
- No changes to library scanning behavior or broader UI redesign beyond the OTP/auth/logging settings shown above.

versions.changelog: Fix: re-added missing Pocket ID preset and other small UI fixes

The hardened OIDC rewrite on Jellyfin 12. Hand-rolled OIDC flow with Trust-On-First-Use discovery-endpoint pinning and an SSRF-guarded, DNS-rebind-pinned HTTP client. Account identity keyed on the OIDC subject, in its own identity-map file (migrated out of the plugin config on upgrade). Fail-closed role-to-policy RBAC with a server-wide admission allowlist. OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0. Client-secret indirection (Client Secret File / ENV_VAR reference). Auto-managed SSO login button in Branding. Rewritten admin config page. Opt-in, per-provider verified-email account linking that never binds an administrator account. Username/email/display-name/email-verified now fall back to the userinfo endpoint when the ID token omits them. Token-validation failures surface a plain-language reason (expired cert, audience/issuer mismatch, clock drift, JWKS rotation) instead of a bare error. Fixed OIDC-authenticated sessions showing a blank IP in Jellyfin's activity log. Fixed the Manage Library Access checkbox not responding to clicks. No configuration migration required from 2.0.0.0. Renamed to SSO-OIDC-Authentication (was SSO-OIDC Authentication) so the install folder no longer mixes a space with a hyphen; your saved settings are unaffected.

BREAKING: requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer will not load on 10.10/10.11 (stay on 1.0.7.x for those). Retargeted to .NET 10 and rebuilt against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin API. Removed the vestigial IAuthenticationProvider.HasPassword override (dropped from the interface in 12.0). No functional changes to the OIDC login, RBAC, or Quick Connect flows.

Security: deny OIDC login when no RBAC role mapping (and no valid Default Role) matches the user's IdP roles, instead of silently letting login through with stale or default permissions — an intentional, unconditional fail-closed behavior change. Fix: declare style-src in the callback page's CSP and nonce the Quick Connect page's inline styles, closing a gap where that page was already CSP-non-compliant. Also: cosmetic redesign of the OIDC callback page (spinner, card layout, dark theme).

Security: evict stale entries from the rate limiter to prevent unbounded memory growth. Security: validate the OIDC picture-claim URL (scheme, host, redirects, size) before fetching it to prevent SSRF via a malicious/compromised IdP or self-service avatar. Security: block login/Quick Connect for a provider disabled mid-flow via an already-issued session token. Security: pin discovery and picture-fetch HTTP connections to the DNS-resolved address AuthorityGuard already validated, closing a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU gap. Also: OIDC callback page CSP now uses a per-response nonce instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

Fix: honor Jellyfin's Base URL setting in generated SSO links (login buttons, branding snippet, callback page) so they work behind a reverse-proxy base path. Feat: sign in native/mobile apps (Android, iOS/Swiftfin, Android TV) via a Quick Connect bridge, since the web login button doesn't reach them. Feat: sync the Jellyfin avatar from the IdP's picture claim on login, with a per-provider opt-out.

Feat: per-IP fixed-window rate limiting on OIDC auth endpoints. Fix: dead-code bug in ClaimParser where JSON array claim values were never parsed. CI: 77-test suite with AAA pattern coverage across all services and controllers.
Fix: role mappings added after a previous save were overwriting earlier ones. Rename plugin to SSO-OIDC Authentication.

versions.changelog: Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

Fixes a small but confusing moment with **Live TV** targets. Live TV has no posters to build a mosaic from, so the **Poster collage** background is unavailable there — and if you had already chosen a collage and then switched the target to Live TV, the background silently changed back to **Image** without a word. The option is now greyed out with a line explaining why, in all three languages, so the change no longer happens behind your back. Nothing else about how covers render has changed.

Adds **Spanish**. The whole configuration page — every step, label, button, hint and message, plus the server's upload and validation errors — is now translated, joining English and Dutch. The page follows your Jellyfin display language, and regional variants come along for the ride: `es-MX` and `es-419` get Spanish just like `es-ES`. Alongside it, the translation files themselves were **cleaned up and put under test**. Roughly a hundred strings left behind by the v3 editor rewrite were still being carried (and would have had to be translated into every new language) — those are gone, and five new build-time checks now fail if a language drifts out of sync with English, if a `{0}` placeholder goes missing, or if a string is defined but never shown. No change to how covers look or render.

Adds an **overlay gradient** to the Background step — a colour that fades in over your background and sits under your text. It is the missing piece behind the look where a poster **resolves into a solid band of colour** at the bottom, with the title on top of it and readable no matter what the poster shows underneath. Each colour stop has its own **opacity**, so you can go from fully transparent to fully solid, use **two colours** for a duotone fade, or wash the whole cover. Four **presets** — Bottom fade, Top fade, Full wash and Duotone — get you there in one click, and switching between them keeps the colours you have already picked so you can try all four without losing your palette. The **Auto palette** swatches now recolour the selected overlay stop, so you can tint a cover with a colour taken straight out of its own artwork. The overlay works with every background type — image, poster collage, gradient or solid — and with animated covers. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The configuration page is now a **guided walkthrough**. Instead of every control at once, designing a cover is laid out as five numbered steps — **Target**, **Background**, **Text & logos**, **Effects**, **Output** — with one open at a time and any of them one click away. Each step shows the controls most people need and keeps the rest under **Advanced**. Choosing a background is now a single choice — **image, poster collage, gradient or solid colour** — instead of a source dropdown plus a separate gradient tick that overlapped with it. The whole page is **properly usable on a phone**: bigger touch targets throughout, the preview pinned at the top while you work, a full-screen poster browser, and canvas handles you can actually grab (they used to shrink to a few pixels on a small screen). Two more additions: **undo and redo** across the whole design with Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, and an **in-context preview** showing your cover wide, square and poster-shaped before you apply it. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

Adds a new **Effects** card. A **colour wash** tints the background under your text, a **vignette** darkens the edges to draw the eye inward, **film grain** adds texture, and a **border** frames the cover — square or rounded, single or double-lined. Every effect is off until you switch it on, and turning one back down to zero leaves your cover exactly as it was. One click of **Jellyfin style** lays down the familiar dark-gradient look with clean white text, which you can then edit freely. And **Auto palette** reads the dominant colours straight out of your background and offers them as swatches — click one to recolour the selected text layer or the colour wash. Existing designs and saved templates are untouched and render exactly as before.

Covers are no longer one line of text. A new **Layers** card lets you stack **as many text layers as you like** plus your own **PNG logos and icons**, each independently styled and freely placed. Every layer can be **shown or hidden, reordered, duplicated, deleted** and selected from the list, and the card below it edits whichever layer you have selected. On the preview canvas, the selected layer gets **corner handles to resize it** and a **knob to rotate it** — hold **Shift** to keep a logo's proportions or snap rotation to 15°. Two new sliders, **Opacity** and **Rotation**, work on text and logos alike. Logos are uploaded the same way as backgrounds (PNG, transparency preserved) and are restored onto the canvas when you load a saved template. As always the server render stays authoritative, and rotated or faded text now renders there exactly as the preview shows it.

Fixes **Reposition background**, which barely worked in 3.0.0.0. Dragging the background now **follows your cursor exactly** — it used to lag badly at low zoom and overshoot at high zoom, matching the cursor only at one specific zoom level. More importantly, repositioning now **works straight away, without zooming in first**: on a **Fill** background you can slide a portrait poster up and down (or a wide still left and right) to choose which part of it the cover shows. Previously that did nothing at all until you zoomed in, because only the zoomed-in part of the image was treated as movable. The server render and the on-screen canvas were fixed together, so what you position is what gets applied. Designs you have already saved or applied are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The config page preview is now a **live interactive canvas**, not a static image: click the title to select it and **drag it** to position, and toggle **Reposition background** to **drag-pan** and **scroll/pinch-zoom** the background image directly on the canvas. A new **Show server render** button renders the exact same design on the server — the authoritative output, since the canvas is a fast approximation — so you can compare before applying. Designs are now stored internally in a new **layered document format** (title text is one layer, more layer types land in a later release); **existing saved templates migrate automatically** the first time you load them, so nothing is lost.

A code-quality and size pass. The plugin is now **much smaller** — the bundled Noto Sans fonts were subset to the glyphs cover titles use (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, punctuation), cutting the plugin DLL from ~3.9 MB to ~1.6 MB with no visible change. **Dead code was removed** (an unused retry service, an unused exceptions module, and nine internal API endpoints the UI never called), and the render pipeline was tidied up (the image compositing is no longer needlessly async). A few **security hardening** touches: the Apply and batch-apply endpoints are now rate-limited and batch size is capped, text size is clamped, poster-collage sources get the same decompression-bomb guard as other images, and error messages no longer echo server paths back to the browser. Purely internal — no user-facing behaviour changes.

Small UI fixes on the Target card: a **disabled button now clearly looks disabled** (dimmed, not-allowed cursor) — the Restore button no longer looks clickable when there's no backup yet — and the Restore row has proper spacing above it. Also added an animated preview to the README.

The **poster browser now covers every library type** — music albums and artists, books, music videos and photos, not just movies and shows — so you can pick a cover from a music or book library too. A **loading spinner** now shows over the preview while it renders, which helps for slower operations like building a poster collage. The **Apply** button now shows an "Applying…" state and locks while it works, so a slow render (like an animated GIF) no longer looks like nothing is happening. **Animated GIF covers are more reliable**: the working size is capped so a full-size render no longer takes forever or fails to apply, and text scales with it so the look is unchanged. The default **Landscape** size is now a lighter 1280×720 (it was 1920×1080) — plenty for library tiles and much smaller files; 1920 is still available via Custom. And the Templates and collage cards were tidied up — the **Delete** and **Shuffle** buttons now sit neatly next to their dropdowns instead of as oversized blocks.

Polish on the v2 release. The config page now matches Jellyfin more closely — compact colour pickers (they used to stretch the full width), and action buttons that align with the selects beside them. The preview no longer starts on a black canvas: it opens with Jellyfin's **brand gradient** (purple → blue) by default. And uploading an **animated GIF** as a background now animates the preview automatically — it switches to Animated GIF output and passes the source's frames through at their own timing, instead of showing a single still frame.

A big release. **Poster-collage backgrounds** build a grid mosaic from a target's own item posters (with density and shuffle controls). **Design templates** let you save a look and reuse it, and **batch apply** pushes one design onto many libraries, collections or playlists at once — each cover titled with its own target's name. **Animated GIF export** is now real: it passes through an animated-GIF background or applies a Ken Burns pan/zoom (capped at 30 frames). And **Restore original cover** reverts any target to its pre-plugin image — applying a cover now backs up the previous image automatically.

The plugin now has its own entry in the dashboard's left navigation menu, so you no longer have to open it through the Plugins list. Added **Live TV** as a cover target (best-effort — it sets the image on Jellyfin's generated Live TV view, which may not persist on every server). Moved the custom-font picker into the **Text** card where it belongs, and added a screenshot to the README.

Fixed the background dim: any non-zero dimming used to black out a picked poster entirely (JPEG posters have no alpha channel, so the overlay painted fully opaque). Dimming now composites correctly and the default was lowered to 0.25. Added an **Image fit** option — Fill (crop), Fit (show the whole image, letterboxed) or Stretch — so a portrait poster no longer gets cropped to a strip in a wide cover. New **multi-colour gradient** picker with an angle control for linear gradients and add/remove colour stops. You can now target **collections** and **playlists** in addition to libraries.

Poster background reliability: authenticate the image download, build the upload without the (sometimes unavailable) File constructor, and surface a clear message at each step so any failure is visible instead of silent.

Fixes. The config page now reliably follows your Jellyfin UI language — the detection reads Jellyfin's stored language setting, not just the browser language (Dutch now shows correctly). Picking a library poster as the background now works: the image is fetched through Jellyfin's own image endpoint and uploaded, instead of resolving a local file path that wasn't always available.

The config page now follows your Jellyfin UI language, with a complete Dutch (NL) translation and English fallback. Font weight now works — all six weights (Light–ExtraBold) are bundled as distinct Noto Sans faces. Background images are cover-fitted instead of stretched, so posters keep their aspect ratio. Added a Landscape 16:9 preset (now the default, best for library covers), a Download button for the generated image, and logging when a background image can't be used.

Redesigned the config page into a native Jellyfin two-column layout with grouped cards and a sticky **live preview** that updates automatically as you adjust settings (no more manual preview button). Styled the file pickers as native buttons showing the chosen file, and made allowed formats and size limits explicit. Fixed the empty library dropdown (libraries now come from GetVirtualFolders). Backfilled earlier version changelogs.

Bundled Noto Sans so titles always render (even on Docker/minimal Linux). Security & correctness hardening: fixed path-traversal and decompression-bomb risks, added rate limiting and font-signature validation, safe colour parsing, image disposal, and generated-file cleanup.
Initial release: custom library cover art with text, gradients, blur, custom backgrounds and fonts, a live preview, and a picker for existing library posters.

Novedades

versions.changelog:
Hotfix for 1.0.7.6 Playability false-positives.

• Removed the bitrate-vs-size pre-filter that flagged efficient x264 rips (YIFY / small MP4 rips of Severance / Landman / Rage / Outlander at 400 MB–2.4 GB) as size-truncated. Decode-check already catches genuine tail-truncation with far fewer false positives.

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Duplicates - new config
- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

TrackFixer's error truncation matches TranscodeFixer now â€” keeps the ffmpeg-error tail (where the real reason lives), not the head.

Transcode fix now actually uses the GPU. v0.9.2 shipped without the hardware-encoder path wired in â€” the UseHardwareEncoder toggle had no effect and every re-encode ran on the CPU via libx265. This release wires the hw path through and adds full VAAPI support (device auto-picked from /dev/dri/renderD* or Jellyfin's VaapiDevice, with format=nv12,hwupload / scale_vaapi in the filter chain). When Jellyfin's own HardwareAccelerationType is unset, the plugin now autodetects: NVIDIA â†’ NVENC, any Linux DRM device (Intel/AMD iGPU or dGPU) â†’ VAAPI, Windows â†’ AMF (or QSV for Intel iGPUs), macOS â†’ VideoToolbox, and falls back to libx265 only when no GPU is present. versions.changelog:
## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.6.6.0
### Fixes
- The lyrics task no longer re-downloads tracks that already have synced lyrics on disk. When a track's lyrics were saved but the database still reported them as plain (Jellyfin doesn't refresh metadata after a download until the next library scan), the task kept "upgrading" the same tracks on every run. It now trusts the synced .lrc file already on disk and skips it. -> #43

## v1.6.5.0
### Fixes
- Build against Jellyfin 10.11.6 instead of always the latest release. Previous builds were linked against 10.11.10 assemblies, which made Jellyfin report the plugin as "not supported" (TypeLoadException) on older 10.11.x servers. The plugin is now compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.6 and newer. -> #55

## v1.6.4.0
### Fixes
- Lyric file detection now also checks Jellyfin's internal metadata folder, not just the media folder. With "Save lyrics into media folders" disabled, already-downloaded lyrics are detected instead of being re-downloaded on every task run, which also reduces load on lrclib.net -> #54

## v1.6.3.0
### What's New
- Optional self-hosted LRCLIB server URL: point the plugin at your own LRCLIB instance instead of lrclib.net. Subpath URLs are preserved and the URL is validated on save. Thanks to @Nausi-llon (#50).
- Built-in rate limiting for lrclib.net requests: enforces a 200 ms minimum gap between calls and honors HTTP 429 `Retry-After` so transient spikes back off cleanly instead of surfacing as per-track errors.
- Identifiable User-Agent on every lrclib request (`jellyfin-plugin-lyrics/<version> (+repo-url)`) so the LRCLIB operators can distinguish this plugin from `jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-lrclib` (#49).

### Notes
- No configuration changes required for existing users — the self-host URL defaults to `https://lrclib.net` and the rate limit only kicks in under load.

## v1.6.2.0
### What's New
- Auto-removes the official "LrcLib Lyrics" plugin (`jellyfin-plugin-lrclib`) on startup if installed, since both plugins register the same lyrics provider and conflict. This plugin is a fork that fixes critical issues — see README. The old plugin can be reinstalled later to switch back.

## v1.6.1.0
### What's New
- Lyrics alternative discovery: skip re-downloading lyrics that already failed in a previous run
- Synced-lyric upgrade now checks the existing sidecar file before replacing plain text

### Fixes
- Stop matching instrumental tracks against unrelated songs: honor LRCLIB's instrumental flag, validate every match against requested duration and artist, and drop the track-name-only fuzzy fallback when artist info is available (#40)
- Scheduled task log: split DB-desync skips from "already synced" skips so plain `.txt` sidecars are no longer counted as synced

### Settings
- New configurable duration-tolerance filter (default on, ±15s) with UI toggle to tune or disable

### Notes
- Jellyfin 10.11.6 or newer is now recommended (see README)

## v1.6.0.0
### What's New
- Added song title cleanup to strip YouTube-style suffixes (Official Music Video, etc.) and duplicate artist names
- Added progressive search fallback: retries with fewer parameters when no results are found
- Added multi-artist support: splits "artist1/artist2" and tries each artist individually
- Replace non-synced lyrics with synced ones when available
- Sped up scheduled lyrics task

### Fixes
- Fixed DI issue with RetryStateStore causing plugin to malfunction on startup
- Fixed fuzzy search failing when album name is missing
- Fixed crash on missing artist or invalid id

### Defaults Changed
- Strict search is now disabled by default
- "Exclude album name" is now enabled by default

## v1.5.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.4.0.0
### What's New
- Added support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.3.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed a lot of plugin loading issues
- Fixed GitHub Action Workflows

### Technical Improvements
- Consistent versioning across all project files
- Better package compatibility with Jellyfin 10.9.x series
- Improved documentation and installation instructions

description:
Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

description:

versions.changelog: 10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Inventory adds one table to the dashboard that lists every item in your libraries with the attributes that matter for storage and quality: size, size per hour of runtime, bitrate, codecs, resolution, HDR and Dolby Vision format, audio layout and languages. Pick the columns you want per media type.

overview: A sortable, filterable table of everything in your libraries.

versions.changelog:
### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

name: StreamLimiter [✓]
overview: Limits the number of simultaneous streams per user.
description:
A Jellyfin plugin that allows you to limit the number of simultaneous streams per user. Features include a default limit, customizable messages, server-side transcode kill for clients that ignore stop commands, and optional device logout.

versions.changelog: Jellyfin 12 build of v1.1.0.0 (same features — see the 1.1.0.0 entry). Servers pick the right build automatically: 10.11 installs 1.1.0.0, Jellyfin 12 installs 1.1.1.0.

- NEW (BETA): HTTP-level hard block — over-limit streams are rejected before any byte is served; works on every client (Swiftfin, Infuse, external players)
- NEW (BETA): single clean custom message on web clients (replaces the built-in dialog)
- NEW: default max streams for users without an explicit limit
- NEW: config migration from pre-1.1 installs (normalizes legacy entries)
- Fixed silent failure where one invalid config entry disabled every limit (#5/#8/#18)
- Fixed device logout (a session id was passed where an access token was expected)
- Kill transcode jobs of blocked streams; optional device logout
- Admin-only stream limit API; removed Newtonsoft.Json
- Fixed duplicated users in the config page dropdown (#16) and empty popup (#6)
- Updated to 10.11 compatible version

- Updated controller 
- Fixed iOS error 
- Fixed configuration management 
- Add TRY in cancel session
- Initial version

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
