versions.changelog:
- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 10.11 - samme rettelse, uden ændringerne fra 12-udgaverne.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

Rettet: et billede fra en film eller serie kunne blive hængende øverst til venstre på siden. Det skete når man trykkede på et kort for noget vi ikke har på serveren, og billedet blev stående - også når man gik tilbage til forsiden.

Forhåndsvisningen (boksen der folder sig ud over et kort) havde mistet sin styling. Et stykke CSS længere oppe i filen manglede alle sine selektorer; det har ligget sådan siden 1.7.0.0 og har aldrig givet noget som helst stil. Men det var ikke bare virkningsløst: browseren læste de løse linjer som én ødelagt regel og slugte den næste rigtige regel sammen med dem - og det var netop den regel der holder forhåndsvisningen usynlig og placerer den fast på skærmen. Uden den blev boksen tegnet som et helt almindeligt element øverst til venstre, fuldt synlig selv når den var lukket. Derfor hjalp det ikke at lukke den.

Det ødelagte CSS er fjernet. Det hørte til den roterende banner der forsvandt i 2.2.0.0, og genre-knapperne har deres egne regler nu, så intet bruger det længere.

Fuld redesign af "Tilføj Film/Serie"-siden. Før: en roterende banner øverst, et tyndt søgefelt og fire vandrette rækker (Seneste anmodninger, Trending, Film, Serier) der hver viste omkring fire titler ad gangen. Nu: søgningen er det første og største på siden, og de fire rækker er erstattet af ÉT gitter, der viser alt på én gang. Alle/Film/Serier og genre-knapperne filtrerer nu det samme gitter i stedet for at være delt op i to næsten ens sektioner, og der er en "Vis flere"-knap. Statusmarkeringerne er lavet om til tre tydelige niveauer: den eneste du kan handle på (Tilføj) er en fremhævet knap, "Anmodet" er en dæmpet mat boble med en langsom puls, og noget der allerede er på serveren viser kun et lille flueben - og selve plakaten tones ned, så øjet springer den over. Titler du allerede har, er som udgangspunkt helt skjult (kan slås til med "Vis dem vi har"), og det du faktisk kan anmode om ligger øverst. Dine egne anmodninger er flyttet fra en stor plakat-række til en kompakt statusliste. Rettet undervejs: Seerr kan returnere flere forskellige titler med samme navn (fx tre udgaver af "Paradise Hotel"), som nu slås sammen til én; og den hårde kant øverst på siden, hvor Jellyfins faste header møder indholdet, er blødt op.

Egne ikoner på de to faner. Tilføj Film/Serie og Udgivelseskalender har nu hvert sit ikon ved siden af teksten, ligesom skins giver Hjem og Favoritter. Ikonet er sat ind som et rigtigt element direkte i knappen frem for inde i tekstelementet, fordi skins tegner deres egne faneikoner med et ::before - og et ::before er selv et flex-element i knappen. Ikonet lander derfor i præcis samme position og arver automatisk den afstand, størrelse og justering det aktive skin i forvejen giver sine egne ikoner. Det tegnes som ligatur med FILL 0, så det får samme tynde streg som resten af rækken i stedet for en massiv variant, og så det ikke kan ramme et forkert glyph hvis skinnet har skiftet ikonskrifttype ud.

Heroen bliver ikke længere klippet af topbjælken. Jellyfins header er position:fixed og højere end det stykke siden lægger fri under den - målt live slutter headeren i 96,7px, mens indholdet begyndte i 81,8px, så de øverste ~15px af fanen lå under bjælken. Det ramte lige præcis heroens hårde, afrundede overkant, hvilket er derfor det så ud som om banneret skar op i topbjælken. Hjem-fanen slap kun udenom fordi dens hero toner sine egne øverste 18% ud, og kalenderfanen fordi den allerede havde topafstand. Anmod-fanen har nu samme 1,6em som kalenderfanen.

Bedre billeder i heroen. Boksen var 4,00:1, mens TMDBs baggrundsbilleder er komponeret i 16:9, så cover smed over halvdelen af billedhøjden væk og viste en tilfældig vandret stribe - med hoveder og horisonter skåret over. Det var derfor de samme billeder så fine ud på et kort, men ikke her. Højden er hævet til 420px (2,86:1), hvilket viser 62% af billedet mod 44% før, og motivet dermed holdes helt. Billederne hentes nu i en opløsning der passer til skærmens pixelforhold i stedet for altid w1280, og de kommende slides forindlæses, så de ikke længere toner ind i en tom boks.

Bygget til at kunne deles. Alle farver aflæses nu fra det tema du kører i stedet for at være hardkodede - den øverste fade var håndmatchet til ElegantFins header-farve og så derfor forkert ud på alle andre temaer. Teksterne følger Jellyfins egen sprogindstilling (dansk/engelsk, eller tvunget), inklusive datoer og "om 3 dage"-linjerne i kalenderen. Nye indstillinger: sprog, Seerr-indigo eller dit eget tema som accentfarve, og til/fra for hver af de to faner. Sproglisten under "Excluded original languages" starter nu tom i stedet for at bortfiltrere 24 sprog som standard. Overskriften over bibliotek-rækken findes nu via dine egne forside-indstillinger i stedet for teksten "Mine medier", så den også virker på andre sprog. Fjernet: en global CSS-regel der ommalede Media Bar-pluginets hero - det hører ikke hjemme i et plugin andre skal installere.

Rettet: skift mellem Hjem/Favoritter og de to indbyggede faner (Tilføj Film/Serie, Udgivelseskalender) endte ofte forkert - typisk på Hjem, eller helt tomt - og krævede flere klik frem og tilbage før den rigtige fane (typisk Favoritter) rent faktisk viste sig. Årsag: koden der finder ud af hvilken Jellyfin-fane der skal vises igen, kiggede efter hvilken native fane-knap DER ER markeret aktiv lige nu - men det er netop den knap, som Jellyfins egen kode først markerer aktiv EFTER klikket, så der opstod et kapløb hvor vores kode nogle gange kiggede for tidligt og enten fandt den forkerte (Udgivelseskalender-fanens egen midlertidigt aktive knap blev fejlagtigt regnet som 'den rigtige'), eller slet ingen. Rettelsen bruger nu direkte det data-index den klikkede knap selv har, i stedet for at gætte ud fra en tilstand der endnu ikke er opdateret.

Fundet og rettet: filmenes udgivelsesdatoer blev stille og roligt lavet om til et forkert format under indlæsning fra Seerr (Newtonsoft.Json genkender automatisk dato-agtige tekststrenge og laver dem om til et DateTime-objekt - som så bliver formateret efter serverens sprogindstilling i stedet for at forblive den oprindelige tekst). Det ødelagde både 14-dages-vinduet og selve sorteringen: en dato som '21-07-2026' sorteres efter alt der starter med '2026-...', så en film der udkommer I DAG endte nederst på listen i stedet for øverst. Bekræftet direkte mod Disclosure Days rigtige data fra Seerr og rettet ved kilden, så det gælder alle datoer kalenderen læser - film, serier og alt andet.

Silo viste sig stadig ikke - hukommelsen fra 1.9.5.0 kan kun huske titler den selv har set mindst én gang, og Silos Seerr-anmodning var allerede væk FØR den udgivelse fandtes. Kalenderen henter nu desuden direkte fra Seerrs egen liste over 'delvist' og 'fuldt tilgængelige' titler (samme status Sonarr/Radarr styrer) - helt uafhængigt af om der findes en aktiv anmodning. Det er en mere robust kilde end anmodningslisten, fordi den ikke kan forsvinde stille og roligt: enhver serie der stadig kører eller lige er blevet færdig og venter på en ny sæson, bliver nu automatisk tjekket for en kommende dato. Ændrer intet ved hvad der reelt vises på kalenderen - stadig kun titler med en ægte dato inden for 14 dage.

Kalenderen glemte titler for tidligt. Rodårsagen bag Silo-sagen: Seerrs egen anmodningsliste kan miste en titel helt, når den bliver fuldt tilgængelig - selvom der stadig er en helt reel, kommende afsnitsdato. Kalenderen har nu sin egen hukommelse over alt den nogensinde har set anmodet gennem Seerr: en titel bliver ved med at blive tjekket for fremtidige datoer, selv efter dens Seerr-anmodning er forsvundet. Hukommelsen vokser automatisk og glemmer kun en titel når en anmodning bevidst fortrydes ('Fortryd'-knappen) - ikke bare fordi Seerr selv har ryddet op. Ændrer intet ved hvad der reelt vises: kun titler med en ægte kommende dato inden for 14 dage kommer stadig på kalenderen.

Rettet: Udgivelseskalenderen kunne blive ved med at vise en serie som 'ingen dato endnu', selvom Seerr selv allerede viste en kommende afsnitsdato. Årsagen var to uafhængige caches: når nogen anmodede eller fortrød noget, genopbyggede pluginet kun den SAMLEDE kalenderliste, men den enkelte titels egne data (op til 12 timer gamle) blev aldrig gjort friske igen - så en dato der lige var dukket op hos Seerr/TMDB, kunne forblive skjult i timevis, selv hen over en 'opdatering'. Anmodninger og fortrydelser rydder nu begge caches, og den passive levetid (når ingen har rørt noget) er sat ned fra 12 til 3 timer. Kalenderen kigger nu også på de 200 seneste anmodninger i stedet for 100.

Kalenderen viser nu et rullende 14-dages vindue: kun film og afsnit med udgivelsesdato inden for de næste to uger vises (emner dukker selv op igen når deres dato kommer i nærheden). Serier uden et planlagt næste afsnit vises ikke længere - kun film uden streaming-dato står på listen under "Dato ukendt endnu". Måneds-overskrifterne er fjernet, så film og serier står i én samlet dato-sorteret liste. Backdrop-kunsten er mere synlig: nedtoningen er trukket ind over tekst-kolonnen, så midten og højre side af kortet viser kunsten næsten klart, og teksten har fået en blød skygge så den stadig er let læsbar. Desuden henter kalenderen nu kun data én gang i døgnet (første åbning efter kl. 04:00) og serveres ellers fra cache - undtagen når der laves eller fortrydes en anmodning via pluginet, hvor den opdaterer med det samme. Anmodninger lavet direkte i Seerrs egen UI dukker først op ved næste kl. 04-opdatering.

Fanen hedder nu "Udgivelseskalender". Rettelse: serier manglede helt. Kalenderen filtrerede alt fra der allerede lå i biblioteket uden en kommende dato - hvilket rammer præcis de igangværende serier der er mellem to sæsoner. Kørende serier vises nu altid, også når næste afsnit endnu ikke er planlagt; kun afsluttede serier der allerede er hentet, udelades. Design: backdrop-kunsten vises nu i fuld styrke og tones kun ned hen over plakat og tekst, så kunsten er tydelig til højre mens teksten stadig er læsbar (teksten kan aldrig løbe ind i det lyse område). Status-mærket ("Behandles") er erstattet af selve udgivelsesdatoen, og kalender-feltet med dag/måned og spørgsmålstegnet i højre side er fjernet.

Nyt design på "Kommer Snart" + fuld sæson-understøttelse for serier. Kalenderen er tegnet om i Seerr's kortsprog - backdrop-kunst bag et kraftigt scrim, plakat, farvede status-pills (Tilgængelig/Behandles/Afventer) og et kalender-felt med dag og måned - men holdt i Jellyfins blå accent og typografi. Serier viser nu ikke bare næste afsnit: sæson-premierer markeres særskilt ("Sæson 3 premiere"), og står der ingen afsnitsdato endnu, bruges sæsonens premieredato i stedet - så en serie mellem to sæsoner ikke fejlagtigt havner under "Dato ukendt". Afsluttede serier siger nu "Serien er afsluttet" frem for at stå tomme. Film er uændret: altid streaming-datoen, aldrig biograf-premieren.

Ny "Kommer Snart"-fane på forsiden. Ved siden af Hjem/Favoritter ligger nu en udgivelseskalender over alt der er ønsket via Seerr - på tværs af alle brugere, så hele husstanden kan se hvad der lander hvornår. Film viser STREAMING-datoen (TMDB's digitale udgivelse), aldrig biograf-premieren; findes der ingen digital dato bruges TV- eller fysisk udgivelse, og ellers havner titlen under "Dato ukendt endnu" i stedet for at vise en misvisende dato. Serier viser næste afsnit med SxxEyy og afsnitstitel - også for serier du allerede har i biblioteket, så "S3E7 på tirsdag" bliver ved med at stå der. Listen er grupperet pr. måned med relativ tekst ("om 3 dage"), og rækker der matcher noget i biblioteket kan klikkes direkte. Datoer caches 12 timer pr. titel, så fanen er hurtig at åbne.

Fix: the 'Mine medier' heading on the home page had reappeared. The hide logic used getElementById('homeTab'), which resolves to whichever mounted home-page instance comes first in the DOM - Jellyfin keeps previously-visited pages mounted with duplicate ids, so the visible page's heading could escape the hide. It now sweeps every mounted home-page instance. Also removed the dead Media Bar overlap-measurement code (Hero Bar's in-flow hero made it obsolete).

Hover-expand card preview: hovering any browse/request card for a moment expands it into a larger preview with backdrop, rating/year/genres, a short description, a Læs mere button linking to the title's IMDb page (TMDB fallback), and the same Tilføj/status action including the Fortryd undo - desktop only, details fetched lazily via the new /SeerrRequests/media/{type}/{id} proxy and cached in-page. Language exclusion: new 'Excluded original languages' setting (comma-separated ISO 639-1 codes, prefilled with East/South/Southeast Asian languages) - browse rows, trending, and the upcoming hero hide matching titles, filtered server-side; explicit search is never filtered. Clear the field to show everything.

Mobile: touch swipe on the upcoming-releases hero, contained so Jellyfin's tab strip doesn't turn a hero swipe into a tab switch; manual slide changes stay in sync with auto-rotation and restart its timer. Genre pills collapse to one horizontally swipeable row on mobile instead of wrapping into several screen-eating rows. Search field pinned to 16px on mobile so iOS Safari stops auto-zooming on focus. Larger pagination-dot touch targets and a tighter phone-sized hero layout.

New: upcoming-releases hero on the Seerr tab. Thin rotating banner above the search field showing upcoming movie and TV releases (from Seerr's discover upcoming endpoints), soonest first, with a Danish release-date pill, title, short overview, and the same Tilføj request flow as the row cards including the Fortryd undo countdown - already-requested or available items show their status badge instead. Clickable pagination dots, 8s crossfade rotation, and the hero stays collapsed at zero height if Seerr is unreachable. New backend proxy endpoint /SeerrRequests/upcoming.

Found the actual root cause of the visible top seam the user kept reporting after two earlier attempts at the fade: it was a color mismatch, exactly as guessed, but the target color was wrong both times. Fetched ElegantFin's own CSS directly and found --headerColor:rgba(30,40,54,.8) (a blue-gray), used inside --headerColorGradient as a gradient that itself already fades to transparent by ~90% of the header's own height - the header was never black or Jellyfin's flat rgb(16,16,16) at all, it just looked that way at a glance. Both this tab's own top gradient and the intensified Hjem hero fade from 1.5.9.0 were using near-black instead, so the header's own fade and the hero/tab fade below it were two differently-toned overlays meeting at a hard edge. Switched both to the same rgba(30,40,54,...) - confirmed with zoomed before/after screenshots on both Hjem and this tab that the seam is gone and the two now read as one continuous fade.

First, ruled out the user's own suspicion that this plugin's CSS might be conflicting with Media Bar or New Badges - confirmed live by fully disabling this plugin's entire stylesheet and checking that Media Bar's hero position/appearance didn't change at all. It doesn't: Media Bar's own fade (.slide .gradient-overlay) is a diagonal-only wash (linear-gradient(130deg,...)), not a top-down fade, so the weak "fade at the top" feeling on Hjem was never a plugin conflict, just how Media Bar's own overlay happens to be designed. Layered a proper vertical dark-to-transparent gradient on top of (not instead of) that existing diagonal one, confirmed via a real screenshot to give Hjem's hero a much more pronounced top fade. Also tightened the Mine medier spacing fix from 1.5.7.0/1.5.8.0 - the +16px buffer used to clear the hero overlap left more empty space than wanted once the actual overlap was gone, brought down to +4px.

The tab-row down-shift and the top gradient still weren't showing up for the user despite two earlier attempts, and they were right - both were genuinely still broken. (1) margin-top on the tab row (tried at .6em then 1.6em) was being mostly absorbed by the header's CSS grid centering (align-items:center) - a computed 23.8px margin-top was only producing a ~2.6px actual visual shift, confirmed precisely via getBoundingClientRect before and after. Switched to position:relative + a plain pixel top offset instead, which isn't subject to that centering interaction at all - confirmed via a real before/after screenshot comparison that the row now visibly clears the logo instead of sitting inline with it. (2) The gradient looked like a floating rectangle instead of a page-wide fade because it was scoped to .sections, which is max-width:1400px + margin:0 auto - the gradient was cutting off at that box's own edges rather than reaching the sides of the window. Moved it to the tab element itself, which isn't width-constrained, so it now spans edge to edge the same way Hjem's own hero does behind its own padded content.

The user pointed out half-window mode already looked perfect (both the fade and the Mine medier spacing), which narrowed this down fast: at a ~1540px window Media Bar's hero (#slides-container) is 750px tall, and Mine medier's row was starting at 631px - a ~210px overlap where the row's own poster art was painting over the bottom of the hero. That's also why the fade looked "missing" specifically at wide windows - it wasn't gone, it was being covered. A fixed padding value couldn't fix this without breaking the already-correct narrower layout, so the row's position is now measured against the hero's actual bottom edge every tick (and on window resize) and only pushed down by exactly the overlap when one actually exists. Also: (1) fixed the Fortryd cancel button showing Anmodet instead of Tilfoej afterward even though the cancellation had genuinely succeeded on Seerr's side - Seerr's DELETE returns 204 No Content with an empty body, which the frontend's own resp.json() call was throwing on, turning a real success into a caught error. (2) Cards in the browse rows brought closer together again (gap now .3em, down from .6em) per feedback that they still felt too spaced out.

Corrections and a new feature: (1) 1.5.5.0 hid the entire Mine medier section by mistake - only the heading text is hidden now, the row of library cards underneath stays visible as intended. (2) The tab row down-shift from 1.5.4.0 was barely visible at full-window widths - confirmed live that .headerTabs is a CSS grid with the tab row centered inline with the logo there (unlike the narrower layout where it sits on its own line below), so a small margin got mostly absorbed. Increased from .6em to 1.6em, confirmed visibly correct at both a ~1540px and an ~800px window. (3) The decorative top gradient added for this tab in 1.5.4.0 turned out to be technically rendering but nearly invisible - too close in tone to the page's own background. Darker and more opaque now, actually reads as a fade. (4) Cards in Trending/Film/Serier/Seneste anmodninger were sitting further apart than intended, and hovering a card near a row's edge clipped its hover-ring glow against the row's own scrollable boundary - reduced the gap and added padding on all sides of each row so the ring has room to render. (5) New: pressing Tilfoej now shows a red Fortryd (undo) button with a live 5 second countdown before settling into the normal Anmodet state, so a mis-click can be reversed instead of leaving a real Seerr request behind. Backed by a new DELETE SeerrRequests/request/{id} endpoint proxying Seerr's own request-cancellation API.

Two more feedback items, shipped before the previous 1.5.4.0 update was even installed: (1) Hides the native Mine medier (My Media) home section - confirmed live this is actually a per-user-configurable Jellyfin home section (the section0 slot), matched here by its heading text rather than that slot class so it stays correct regardless of how sections are ordered. Worth knowing this can also be turned off directly in Jellyfin's own Display preferences > Home screen sections, no plugin needed - hidden here anyway since it was asked for directly. (2) The custom scrollbar added in 1.5.3.0 for Trending/Film/Serier/Seneste anmodninger turned out not to be wanted after all - the bar itself is now hidden (scrollbar-width:none / ::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}) while the underlying overflow-x:auto scrolling stays fully functional via mouse-wheel, trackpad, touch, or drag.

Feedback round: (1) Removed the quality/season picker popup entirely - it never rendered reliably enough to be worth keeping, so Tilfoej now submits the request immediately at the fixed default (1080p, all seasons for TV) instead. Also removed the now-unused tv-seasons backend endpoint and Seasons request field. (2) The Behandles loading dots now bounce once per dot in quick succession near the start of a 5 second cycle, then go quiet until the next one, instead of bouncing continuously every ~1 second. (3) Confirmed live that Media Bar's own slideshow (a fixed element parented directly to body) only renders while the native Hjem tab content is actually active - it isn't broken by this plugin, it's correctly scoped to the real home tab and hides behind this one. Added a purely decorative dark-to-transparent gradient at the top of this tab instead, so it doesn't look as flat compared to Hjem's own hero backdrop. (4) The Jellyfin wordmark in the header (not a link anywhere in Jellyfin's own markup) now navigates back to Hjem when clicked, from any top-level page where it's shown - non-home pages already have Jellyfin's own native Hjem button in its place, so this only needed wiring where the static logo is what's actually visible.

Found that 1.5.2.0's fixed-delay retries (rAF + 50ms + 200ms) for cancelling the stuck dialog entrance animation still weren't a wide enough net - live testing showed Jellyfin's MutationObserver can attach the animation later than 200ms, so the dialog was still confirmed stuck at opacity:0 after the previous fix. Switched to a bounded polling loop (checks every 120ms for about 4 seconds, cancelling whenever an animation is found) which reliably catches it regardless of when it lands. Also five feedback-driven changes: (1) the whole Hjem/Favoritter/Tilfoej Film/Serie tab row is nudged down slightly instead of sitting flush against the very top edge. (2) Every card action state - the Tilfoej button and the Tilfoejet/Anmodet/Behandles badges - now shares one consistent bottom-center slot on the poster instead of badges living top-left while the button lived bottom-center. (3) Behandles now shows three small dots that bounce in sequence, a loading-style cue instead of a static label. (4) Trending/Film/Serier/Seneste anmodninger rows switched from the native is="emby-scroller" (which turned out to scroll via a JS transform, not real overflow - there was never an actual native scrollbar to restyle) to a plain overflow-x:auto row with a custom-styled indigo scrollbar, replacing the previous prev/next arrow buttons with real mouse-wheel/trackpad/touch scrolling plus a visible modern scrollbar. (5) More breathing room between the search field/results and Seneste anmodninger.

Found the actual cause of the popup that kept looking dim/washed-out across 1.5.0.0 and 1.5.1.0, despite the background genuinely being solid: Jellyfin's own core JS auto-attaches a Web Animations API entrance animation (opacity 0 to 1, scale .96 to 1, 180ms) to any element matching the native dialog class pattern, independent of whether it was opened through Jellyfin's real dialogHelper. Confirmed live via dialog.getAnimations() that this animation gets stuck permanently at its 0%-progress frame - opacity:0 - and never completes, leaving the entire popup invisible/near-invisible instead of just dim. The dialog now proactively cancels this animation right after being inserted (with a couple of staggered retries, since Jellyfin attaches it asynchronously), which reverts the element to its normal CSS-resolved opacity:1 instantly. Also dropped the dialog-fixedSize class the popup didn't actually need (it duplicates constraints already set with !important) - as a side effect this also stopped the ElegantFin theme's own dialog-fixedSize override from forcing square corners on the popup at most window sizes. Two smaller fixes: the Tilføj button now scales up slightly on hover, and items already on the server show a green "Tilføjet check" badge instead of "Tilgaengelig", both in the browse rows and in Seneste anmodninger.

Fix a regression from 1.5.0.0: the new bottom-gradient scrim added a #seerrRequestsTab .cardImageContainer{position:relative} rule to give the ::after scrim a positioning context, but .cardImageContainer is already position:absolute natively (that's what stretches it to fill the aspect-ratio box .cardPadder-overflowPortrait creates via padding-bottom) - our ID-scoped rule had higher specificity than that single-class native rule, silently downgrading it to relative and collapsing every card (Trending/Film/Serier/search/recent-requests) to zero height. Confirmed live: no artwork, no visible or clickable request buttons anywhere in the tab, even though the underlying data and DOM were all correct. Removed the unnecessary position override - position:absolute already gives descendants a valid positioning context, so the scrim didn't need it. Also renamed the request button from "Anmod" to "Tilføj" (and its in-progress/dialog-header/error text to match), for consistency with the "Tilføj Film/Serie" tab button's own wording.

Three fixes based on feedback: (1) Pressing the browser Back button while the Seerr tab was active (e.g. after clicking a Tilgængelig item's link to its Jellyfin details page) left the home page broken, showing only our content and whatever other plugins render outside the tab structure. Root cause: Jellyfin's router only restores the active TAB BUTTON's highlighted state on route re-entry, not the actual is-active class on the content div - that swap normally only happens as a side effect of a real tab-button click, and returning via Back never clicks anything. Now listens for hashchange (not just native tab-button clicks) and explicitly restores whichever native tab's content div matches the currently active button's data-index. (2) The request/season/quality popup looked washed-out - confirmed live its background was only 90% opaque over an already-translucent backdrop, inherited from the theme's own dialog styling meant for bigger dialogs, not a small popup. Forced fully opaque. Also confirmed the popup wasn't reliably centered by the native flex-centering it was relying on, so it's now explicitly centered and capped at min(420px, 92vw) with a tighter phone-width layout, instead of stretching toward the native dialog's full width on smaller windows. (3) Light visual pass to blend Seerr's own look with the Jellyfin theme: consistent indigo accent color across the request button, active genre pills, search focus ring, and popup borders; small accent bars on section titles; a bottom gradient scrim on every poster so badges/buttons stay legible against bright art.

Feedback round: (1) The Anmod button is now a rounded indigo pill centered at the bottom of the poster, matching Seerr's own request-button placement/color, instead of the New-Badges-style top-left corner pill (status badges like Tilgængelig/Anmodet stay top-left). (2) Removed the auto-detected 4K-capability check from 1.3.0.0 - it correctly found that this Seerr instance's single Radarr/Sonarr server reports is4k:false and so was silently always skipping the prompt, but the user confirmed that one server actually handles both 1080p and 4K, so the quality popup is now always shown on every request instead of gating on a server flag that doesn't reflect real capability here. (3) TV requests now open a proper season picker first (fetched via a new /tv-seasons/{tmdbId} endpoint, mirroring Seerr's own request modal) with per-season checkboxes, a Vælg alle toggle, and already-available/requested seasons shown disabled - only the checked seasons are sent instead of always requesting seasons:"all".

Major redesign based on feedback: (1) No longer a separate full-page takeover - integrated as a real home-page tab exactly like Favoritter. Confirmed live that Favoritter never changes the URL, it just toggles an is-active class between sibling .tabContent.pageTabContent divs that Jellyfin keeps permanently mounted inside the home page - the browse panel now works the same way, so you never leave the home page at all. Also found and fixed that clicking a native tab (Hjem/Favoritter) doesn't automatically hide a foreign sibling tab-content div, so a click watcher on the tab row now handles that side explicitly. (2) Split the old single filterable 'Udforsk' grid into three separate always-visible horizontally-scrollable rows - Trending, Film, and Serier - matching the native home page's own row style, each with its own contextual genre filter pills instead of one global type toggle. (3) Requesting now prompts for 1080p vs 4K via a small popup dialog, but only when this Seerr instance actually has a 4K-flagged Radarr/Sonarr server configured (checked via a new /quality-options endpoint) - no point asking a question with only one real answer.

Feature round based on feedback: (1) Subtle slow animated gradient on the page background instead of a flat fill. (2) Fixed 'Seneste anmodninger' not lining up with 'Udforsk' - the native emby-scroller used for the recent-requests row carries its own 23px left padding that the plain discover grid doesn't, now overridden. (3) Items marked Tilgængelig now link straight to their Jellyfin details page - Seerr's own MediaInfo already tracks the linked jellyfinMediaId once something becomes available, no extra lookup needed. (4) Anmod button and status badges restyled as small top-left corner pill badges matching New Badges' own NEW ribbon/rank badge look, instead of a full-width bottom bar. (5) Udforsk now supports Load more pagination using Seerr's page/totalPages fields. (6) Added an Alle/Film/Serier filter row plus contextual genre pills (fetched from Seerr's /genres/movie and /genres/tv) to filter the Udforsk suggestions.

Fix: the 'Tilføj Film/Serie' button could vanish permanently after opening the full page and going back. Button injection cached an 'already injected' flag and skipped re-checking once true, but Jellyfin rebuilds the Hjem/Favoritter tab row's contents on any hashchange - including toggling the ?seerrRequests=1 flag on and back off - even though the underlying route (#/home) never changes, silently wiping the button out from under the stale flag. Removed the flag entirely; the DOM presence check itself is cheap enough to just always run.

Two changes based on feedback: (1) Replaced the floating dialog with a real full-page view. The old modal stacked a translucent dialog body (90% opaque) on top of a translucent backdrop (66% opaque) - both native Jellyfin dialog conventions - which compounded into a noticeably dim, washed-out look. The panel now opens as a solid full-viewport page (matching the app's own #101010 background) toggled by a hash flag on the current route (#/home?seerrRequests=1) rather than a real new route, since navigating to an actually-unrecognized hash renders Jellyfin's own 'Side ikke fundet' error page - this way the browser back button and URL both work like real navigation without fighting Jellyfin's router. (2) The 'Tilføj Film/Serie' button was visibly slower to appear than the native Hjem/Favoritter tabs next to it, because button injection was gated behind the same 400ms debounce used for heavier scan work. It's now a plain cheap idempotency check that runs immediately on every DOM mutation instead.

Fix: the 'Tilføj Film/Serie' button never actually appeared next to Hjem/Favoritter - .tabs-viewmenubar turned out to live in Jellyfin's shared app header (.skinHeader), a sibling of .page.homePage, not a descendant of it, so scoping the search to the active home page found nothing. Now searches the document directly (isHomeRoute() already prevents it from firing while some other section's tab row is showing instead). Live-verified end to end after the fix: button renders in the right spot, click doesn't trigger a tab switch, and search/discover/recent-requests all return correctly enriched data.

Fix: every endpoint returning Ok(new JObject{...}) was silently corrupted - ASP.NET Core's default System.Text.Json output formatter has no built-in support for Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JObject, and since JObject also implements IEnumerable, it got serialized as an empty array instead of an object (confirmed live: {"ok":true,"version":"3.3.0"} came back as {"ok":[],"version":[]}). All JObject responses now go through a small helper that renders them via Newtonsoft's own ToString() as a raw ContentResult instead, the same way the Seerr proxy passthroughs already worked correctly.

Fix: the config page's embedded <script> never actually executed on this server (Jellyfin's dashboard loads plugin config pages via a mechanism that drops inline scripts), so the Save button's submit handler never attached and clicking it fell through to a native form submission - which leaked the Seerr API key into the browser URL as a plaintext query string. The Save/Test connection form no longer uses a <form>/type="submit" at all, and all of its load/save/test-connection logic now lives in inject.js instead (already proven to load reliably, since it's injected into index.html itself rather than fetched as a page fragment).

Initial release. Adds a 'Tilføj Film/Serie' button to the home page tab row that opens a themed panel with search, a 'Seneste anmodninger' (recent requests) row, and an 'Udforsk' (browse/trending) grid, all backed by a Seerr instance configured in the plugin's settings page (base URL + admin API key). Requests are proxied server-side (avoids CORS entirely) and attributed to the requesting household member's own Seerr account via Seerr's Jellyfin-user lookup, when they've linked one - falls back to the shared admin account otherwise.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

The category is not free text. The official catalogue uses exactly eight values, and one outside that set parses cleanly and then belongs to no filter at all - the plugin would quietly drop out of every category view with no error anywhere. The build now refuses a value outside those eight before it starts, rather than shipping one and finding out later.

Only the repository manifest is actually read for this, so it could have been changed without a release. Added: two centred badge positions, "Top, centred" and "Bottom, centred", for images a client crops on the sides. Jellyfin's episode list shows a still in a container of its own proportions and takes the difference off the left and right, so a badge near either edge is cut in half - and raising the margin does not help, because the crop is proportional rather than a fixed number of pixels.

Centred sidesteps that instead of fighting it: the crop may take as much as it likes off both sides and a badge in the middle stays whole, so only the vertical distance still has to fit. The horizontal margin is ignored in these two positions, because a margin is a distance from an edge and there is none. With a vertical badge direction each pill is centred on its own rather than the column as a block.

Existing presets are unaffected: the new values are appended, so the four corners keep the meaning they had.

Changed: a folder that says two independent things now gets two edition badges. "REMASTERED.EXTENDED" used to draw EXT alone, because both rules matched and only the first was ever used.

Collecting every match would be wrong the other way round - it would turn "Extended Directors Cut" into three badges for one version. So each rule now declares what kind of statement it makes: which cut this is, how the picture is framed or coloured, how the copy was mastered. Within one kind the first match still wins, so a combination like EDC stays a single badge; across kinds the badges stand side by side, with the cut first because that is what tells two copies of a film apart.

Measured over 2380 real folders, six carry two edition tokens and no folder carries two of the same kind, so this is a small and predictable change.

versions.changelog:
## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Nothing runs for non-admins**: the script checks who you are first, instead of every user's browser polling once a minute for an admin-only answer.
- **Far fewer checks**: every five minutes instead of every minute, and paused while the tab is in the background.
- **Smaller checks**: each check now asks only for the number it needs, instead of downloading every plugin's full release notes and throwing them away.
- **Switching tabs is free**: returning to the Jellyfin tab no longer triggers a fresh check.
- **Lighter on the browser**: the plugin now only keeps an eye on the page while a notification is actually showing, rather than constantly, for everyone.

## 📋 Notes

- The badge can now take up to five minutes to appear after a plugin is updated, rather than up to one. Opening the user menu always shows the current count.

## ✨ New Features

- **Plugin icon**: the plugin now has its own icon in the catalog and in your plugin list, instead of a blank placeholder.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Readable changelogs**: a plugin's release notes on the **Plugin Updates** page now appear properly formatted. Bold text, headings and links show as intended, instead of displaying the raw formatting characters around them.

## 📋 Notes

- Nothing to reconfigure. Updating takes only the usual restart.
- Still Jellyfin 12 only. The avatar badge and profile-menu entry need the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin; the dashboard page works without it.

## Plugin Update Notifier 1.0.0.0

First release, for Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin installs plugin updates in place but only applies them on the next server restart, and nothing in the UI tells an administrator that a restart is pending. This plugin closes that gap: it watches plugin install and update events and surfaces a clear, dismissible reminder until the server is restarted.

### Features

- Avatar badge: a dot appears on the admin's profile avatar the moment a plugin change leaves a restart pending.
- Profile-menu entry: a "Plugin Updates" item in the user dropdown, shown only to administrators, with a count of what changed.
- Dashboard page: lists every changed plugin, its old and new version, the release changelog, and a link to each plugin's source.
- Shared dismiss: dismissing hides the reminder for every admin session, not just one browser; a later plugin change brings it back.
- Self-clearing: the reminder disappears on its own after the restart it was asking for.

### Requirements

- Jellyfin 12 (this release uses APIs not present in 10.x).
- The avatar badge and profile-menu entry additionally require the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin (4.0.0.0 or newer). The dashboard page works without it.

versions.changelog:
# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.

versions.changelog:
Same plugin as v12.0.1.0 - no functional changes. It exists so that servers
upgraded from Jellyfin 10.11 to Jellyfin 12 automatically pick up the correct
build.

Bug Fixes:
- Upgrading Jellyfin from 10.11 to 12 left the plugin showing "Not supported".
  Each release published its 10.11 and its 12 build under the same version
  number, so a server that had installed the 10.11 build kept it after the
  upgrade - Jellyfin saw no newer version to offer, and the 10.11 build cannot
  run on Jellyfin 12. This release is published for Jellyfin 12 only, so those
  servers now see an update and repair themselves. Jellyfin 10.11 servers are
  unaffected and stay on v12.0.1.0.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

The first stable release for Jellyfin 12, and the biggest update yet - 22 release
candidates of work since v10.11.30.2. Jellyfin 10.11 is still fully supported.

Jellyfin 12:
- Full support for Jellyfin 12, including the final 12.0.0 release
- Jellyfin 10.11 continues to receive the same updates

New features:
- List templates: one-click starting points on the Create tab
- Hide when empty: a list disappears while nothing matches, and returns on its own
- Group results into collections: turn an item search into a collection of collections
- Collection and Playlist media types: build collections of collections or playlists
- Smart collections now carry genres, studios, parental rating and total runtime
- Smart list badge on generated covers, with a setting to turn it off
- Integration API so other tools can create and manage smart lists
- Bumpers, and random group selection
- New rule field: User Rating
- Date rules can include items whose date is missing from metadata
- New settings for default media types and for hiding new lists when empty

External lists:
- New providers: ListenBrainz and Scrob
- Music lists match tracks via MusicBrainz, one library item per matched track
- User-Agent setting for when a provider starts blocking requests

Sorting:
- Least Recently Watched Round Robin, and Shuffled Round Robin
- Round Robin can group by Collection and order items within each group
- Crossover episodes that aired close together play back-to-back, with an Air Window setting
- Play Count (all users) and Last Played (all users)

Improvements:
- Large speed-up for expensive rules - people, languages, resolution and more are read once per refresh
- Parent tags, studios and genres are found at every level above an item, including the library
- Only fully watched episodes advance the Least Recently Watched rotation
- Weekly cleanup removes leftover playlists and collections whose list is gone
- Rule groups are named consistently throughout; the sort option is now Rule Group Order

Bug fixes:
- Titles containing numbers sort correctly - "Season 2" before "Season 10"
- The Resolution sort did nothing and left lists sorted by name
- Episodes came back unordered when Season/Episode was combined with another sort
- A series showed a play count of 0 even when every episode was watched
- Items with no release date no longer match "before", "older than" and "not equals"
- IMDb lists, charts and awards failed to load with a "Forbidden" error
- Configuration pages loaded blank behind a reverse proxy, or with Cloudflare Rocket Loader
- Smart collections disappeared when the TMDbBoxSets plugin was installed
- Duplicates left behind by a failed deletion are detected and cleaned up
- List names can contain : * ? < > | " / and \ again
- Saving a list now reports why it failed instead of appearing to do nothing
- A failed save no longer discards what you typed
- Deleting a list right after editing it no longer brings it back

Existing lists may change:
- Rules checking parent values now look at every level above an item, so they match more
- Music lists are the most visible case: artist folder and library values now count
- Similar To applies within its own rule group instead of filtering the whole list
- Smart collections now carry aggregated genres/studios/runtime, so other lists may match them
- Include-only checkboxes are migrated automatically to Name rules

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

versions.changelog: Reuse the successful native media classification attached to an authorized proxy lease for later large seek requests. Avoid repeated byte-zero classification reads that can stall after an origin has already accepted the requested range, while retaining range validation, representation validator checks, HLS rewriting, exact source identity and fail-closed behavior. Add regressions proving that large seeks skip the redundant classification request and still reject changed representations. Verified with 586 tests and the complete owned Jellyfin integration workflow.

Preserve the exact opened native source for Jellyfin remux, HLS and seek requests after discovery withdrawal by binding a private source snapshot to the user, PlaySessionId and native version. Reuse the already-authorized opaque proxy lease, revalidate permissions, ownership, content and session identity, and fail closed without substituting another version. Add controlled Jellyfin 12.1 coverage for progressive and nested HLS playback, seeking, decoded audio/video and playback revocation. Verified with 584 tests and the complete owned Jellyfin smoke workflow.

Avoid overlapping classification and media responses within a playback relay request. Classify long byte-zero reads in place and finish prefix classification before seeks or short ranges. Preserve HLS rewriting, exact source selection, authorization and SSRF safeguards; reject conflicting advertised representations and invalid ranges. Add credential-free stage and cause diagnostics for relay failures. Verified with 578 tests and real Jellyfin playback, including bounded reads at 6 GiB and generated HEVC/AAC seeking. Independent FFmpeg requests can still overlap; the reported production NAS failure is not yet verified resolved.

Route native FFmpeg and ffprobe reads through Jellyfin's bound local HTTP address and port instead of the public reverse proxy, while preserving public playback URLs for clients. Keep rewritten HLS playlists, segments and keys on the reader's origin and base path. Avoid reopening and probing an already-probed selected version during remux and seek. Preserve capability authorization, account isolation, range validation and private-host safeguards. Includes regression and real Jellyfin coverage with an unreachable public playback hostname.

Identify failed catalog subscriptions in Tasks and synchronization history with stable identities and safe causes, persisted across restarts without exposing credentials or upstream errors. Partial synchronization still reports Failed and preserves prior media. Fix equivalent GUID handling and keep non-playable metadata available for canonical and retired versions so native progress/stop reports can save resume state without reopening retired sources or crossing user boundaries. Adds English/French failure details and regression coverage for catalog preservation, safe persistence and playback reporting.

Fix a Jellyfin startup regression when an existing Siphon catalog exceeds 256 MiB. Large valid state files load and save without truncation, preserving native identities, ownership and metadata; the 100,000-item limit and atomic writes remain enforced. Prevent calendar notification starvation under brief publication-lock contention and create generated native collections with their initial members, preserving manual additions. Correct native login and notification smoke synchronization, allow matching source/catalog versions after publication, update the Node.js action runtime, and pin Linux CI to Ubuntu 24.04. Detailed release notes now come from annotated tags rather than a tracked notes file.

Siphon 1.5.0.0: private user addon profiles, native collections and saved additions, selected-version HTTP/P2P downloads, source and metadata diagnostics, selective history recovery, followed-series calendar and opt-in notifications, targeted synchronization, provider quotas and shared caching, IntroDB timings, and bounded opt-in P2P playback. Includes media-response validation and the unchanged supplied icon. Persistent offline queues, offline HLS exports and external webhooks remain unreleased 1.6 features.

FIX: TrackChangeController made fully async — removed .GetAwaiter().GetResult() that caused thread pool starvation and request deadlocks
FIX: Duplicate suppression — same track reported within 15 seconds is suppressed (handles Liquidsoap firing on_track multiple times per play)
FIX: Removed backward drift correction — it caused duplicate track sends to Liquidsoap queue, making playlists longer than expected
FIX: Schedule change now takes immediate priority — RefillQueueAsync aborts if schedule changed, preventing old playlist from continuing past its time slot
IMPROVE: GetCurrentlyPlayingIndexAsync replaces VerifyPositionAsync — only detects stuck tracks, no longer modifies _nextTrackToSend counter

CRITICAL FIX: Liquidsoap stuck detection — when Liquidsoap stops advancing (codec error, corrupt file), the plugin no longer spams queue.append every 5 seconds in an infinite drift correction loop
FIX: VerifyPositionAsync now returns current track index to RefillQueueAsync for stuck detection
FIX: RefillQueueAsync pauses queue refill when Liquidsoap is stuck (same track across consecutive checks)
FIX: Automatically resumes normal refill when Liquidsoap advances past the stuck track
FIX: ResetState clears stuck state (_isStuck, _lastKnownCurrentIdx)

FIX: Position verification compares Liquidsoap reality (current_track + queue.length) vs plugin counter to detect skipped tracks
FIX: Playlist now loops automatically when all tracks exhausted but schedule is still active — prevents dead air
IMPROVE: VerifyPositionAsync runs as part of RefillQueueAsync cycle — minimal overhead (one extra Telnet query)

NEW: No Content-Disposition header — displays inline in browser instead of downloading

FIX: Replaced ResetState() with _nextTrackToSend=0 to only reset the send index without destroying the loaded playlist
ROOT CAUSE: In v0.0.0.37, _playlistTracks was set at line 411, then ResetState() at line 431 cleared it — queue.append was never called

FIX: _currentScheduleKey now only set on successful queue, cleared on failure so next cycle retries automatically
IMPROVE: Error message now includes 'will retry on next cycle' for clarity

SIMPLIFY: LiquidsoapClient — removed OnReconnected event, HadPreviousConnection, GetQueueRemainingAsync
IMPROVE: Buffer refill based on queue.length instead of estimated timing — 100% reliable
IMPROVE: Resume on restart still works via queue.current_track + queue.length query
IMPORTANT: You MUST add on_track HTTP callback to radio.liq — see release notes
IMPORTANT: Remove queue.remaining command from radio.liq (no longer needed)

FIX: Plugin restart no longer resets playback to track 0 - on fresh start, queries what Liquidsoap is actually playing and resumes from that position (no audio interruption)
FIX: _currentTrackIndex desync eliminated on restart - Liquidsoap keeps playing uninterrupted while the plugin repositions its tracking to match
NEW: TryResumeCurrentPlaylistAsync - queries queue.current_track on startup, matches against playlist, and resumes tracking from the correct position

- Your selected voice track stays selected when moving to the next episode, including choices made through Jellyfin's standard version selector.

- Improved playback recovery after temporary loading failures.
- Reduced unnecessary load during library refreshes.
- Fixed issues with episode information and available voice tracks.

Requires Jellyfin 10.11.

## What changed

- Added a complete series voice selector that includes translations available through Jellyfin versions and all supported providers, including Kodik-only coverage.
- A selected voice now stays active across episodes: Jellyfin `Next` and autoplay advance in that voice wherever it is available. `Auto` restores normal automatic selection.
- Improved playback recovery for Alloha, CVH, and Kodik streams, including temporary provider failures, expired stream resources, stalls, and quality fallback.
- Added more accurate episode runtimes and earlier intro/outro skip availability when provider metadata is available.
- Made repeated library refreshes substantially faster when titles and generated files are unchanged, while still rechecking provider coverage when needed.
- Improved mixed-provider libraries where one provider has only part of a season or a translation is available from a different provider.
- Added an optional safe cleanup setting for plugin-managed releases removed from a successfully fetched Yummy user list. It is disabled by default.

## Compatibility

- Requires Jellyfin 10.11.x and .NET 9, unchanged from the previous release.
- Existing plugin configuration remains compatible. The old Jellyfin server base URL value is retained for compatibility but is no longer used or shown; generated streams now use Jellyfin's local gateway automatically.
- Voice selection is series-wide because Jellyfin stores the primary episode version globally. Different users cannot keep independent simultaneous voice locks for the same series.

## After updating

- Replace or install the plugin files, then restart Jellyfin.
- Run `Scheduled Tasks -> YummyKodik library refresh` once. The first refresh can take longer because generated metadata and refresh state are upgraded.
- Scan the Jellyfin library that points at the generated folder after that refresh.
- Use `Auto` in the series voice selector before making a one-off choice through Jellyfin's native version selector.

## What changed

- Made library refresh faster while keeping external API pressure conservative. Refresh workers can process different titles in parallel, but the default limit remains 2.
- Added a single-run gate so a second refresh exits quickly instead of doing duplicate work.
- Added per-series filesystem locks so season folder migration, cleanup, STRM/NFO writes, and state writes are serialized for the same series root.
- Split the refresh flow into smaller services for title loading, metadata writing, episode generation, Kodik supplementing, state checks, and cleanup.
- Added refresh state files for safe single-file skips. State is multi-season, written atomically, and never stores raw provider tokens, cookies, bearer tokens, or secret-bearing URLs.
- Added strict skip validation. The plugin now checks fingerprints, covered episodes, managed file hashes, missing files, and stale episode-shaped artifacts before skipping a title.
- Kept per-voice mode conservative. It still runs full provider lookup so new voice translation files can appear even when episode counts do not change.
- Made corrupt, missing, stale, or ambiguous refresh state fall back to a full refresh instead of failing or skipping too aggressively.
- Improved stale artifact cleanup for generated episode STRM/NFO files, including zero-episode and future-episode cases.
- Improved legacy season folder and episode filename migration under the series-root lock.
- Fixed atomic text writes so existing read-only generated STRM/NFO files can be replaced during refresh.
- Made Shikimori layout caching safe for concurrent refresh workers.
- Made shared Kodik token and lookup paths safer under parallel refresh and runtime playback.
- Delayed Kodik client initialization until a title actually needs Kodik supplement data.
- Added refresh performance diagnostics for slow-stage and file-operation troubleshooting.
- Added a configurable Minimum plugin log level. The default is Warning, so normal refresh and playback no longer spam Jellyfin with informational YummyKodik logs.
- Fixed a logging startup regression by avoiding global ILogger replacement and filtering only YummyKodik loggers.
- Improved Alloha/CVH/Kodik fallback handling, voice matching, playlist proxy recovery, and token refresh behavior used by runtime playback.
- Added regression coverage for refresh state skips, stale artifacts, parallelism, run gate behavior, thread-safe Shikimori cache, atomic file replacement, and plugin log filtering.

## After updating

- Restart Jellyfin after the plugin update.
- Open YummyKodik settings and verify Output root path and Jellyfin server base URL.
- Leave Minimum plugin log level at Warning for quiet normal operation, or lower it to Information/Debug/Trace only while diagnosing an issue.
- In Docker, use container paths such as /media/yummykodik, not Windows host paths.
- Run Scheduled Tasks -> YummyKodik library refresh after changing slugs, user-list settings, ServerBaseUrl, or per-voice STRM mode.
- Scan the Jellyfin library that points at the generated folder.

## What changed

- Added blended provider coverage across Alloha, CVH, and Kodik. Users choose the anime source and desired quality; the plugin combines all available provider data to create as many episode files as possible.
- Added provider failover: if an episode is missing from one provider, one provider has fewer episodes, or playback resolution fails, the plugin can use a neighboring provider instead.
- Added Jellyfin Web `seriesTranslation.js` voice widget on series pages. It shows Auto plus available voices and saves a per-user, per-series choice.
- Fixed normal single-file mode voice preferences so a choice made in the widget is shared across Alloha/CVH-backed episode URLs and can route playback to the provider that actually has the selected voice.
- Added optional per-voice STRM generation so Jellyfin can show separate episode versions for different voice translations.
- Added intro/outro media segments from Yummy/Kodik skip timings for Jellyfin clients that support skip actions.
- Added automatic Kodik token resolution and refresh, while keeping manual token override support.
- Improved season/title layout resolution using Yummy viewing order and Shikimori metadata, including specials and multi-season titles.
- Improved generated file maintenance: stale artifacts are cleaned up, equivalent translation names are normalized, and duplicate Kodik episode links are deduplicated.
- Fixed Docker/base-image compatibility by targeting Jellyfin 10.11.0 shared assemblies.
- Fixed Docker/server URL handling so a trailing slash in ServerBaseUrl does not create //YummyKodik playback URLs.

name: JellyToneDown [✓]
description:
Jellyfin plays a theme song in the background when you open a series or a movie, and offers no way to turn it down. JellyToneDown adds one. A server-wide default plus optional per-user levels, applied to theme songs and the audio of theme videos and to nothing else. The adjustment is made on the server, so it reaches every client - the web player, Swiftfin, Findroid, the Android TV app, Kodi and Infuse alike - rather than only the ones that happen to expose a volume control. Files in your library are never modified; adjusted copies live in Jellyfin's cache. The plugin does not download, assign, rename or otherwise manage theme music. It only changes how loud it is.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 23:13 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raleighawes0me/JellyToneDown/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/raleighawes0me/JellyToneDown
overview: Adjust the volume of theme music. Just that.

versions.changelog:
- The in-browser slider is now labelled **All themes**, and carries a tooltip saying it applies
  to every title and to your account only. It always worked that way; appearing over a
  particular series just made it look like a per-series control.
- The per-user settings page says the same thing in the same words.
- The slider now stays up for as long as a theme is actually playing, instead of fading after a
  few seconds. Previously, once it had gone there was no way to get it back for the theme
  already playing short of opening a different title. It still fades a few seconds after the
  theme stops, and hovering it keeps it up as before.
- On narrow screens the panel now drops the percentage rather than the "All themes" label, so
  the thing that says what the slider controls survives on a phone.

- The in-browser volume slider no longer needs a writable web client. The script tag is now
  added to `index.html` as the page is served, by middleware, instead of being written into
  the file on disk. That was the one part of the plugin that did not work on a normal package
  install, where the web client is owned by root and Jellyfin runs as its own user - and it
  also means a Jellyfin upgrade can no longer undo it.
- The old on-disk patch is still selectable under **Web client -> How the script gets in**, and
  switching away from it removes anything it previously wrote.
- The config page now reports how many page loads the script has actually been added to, rather
  than only whether it is switched on.
- The catalogue icon is no longer a square that Jellyfin blew up to fill the card.

- Fixed the per-user settings page always reporting an expired session. Jellyfin 12 ships a
  migration that disables legacy authorization, which switches off the `X-Emby-Token` header
  the page was authenticating with. It now uses the standard `Authorization: MediaBrowser`
  scheme.
- Added a plugin icon.
- Per-version release notes: every version used to read "Initial release" in the catalogue.

- Added a per-user settings page at `/JellyToneDown/MySettings`, so users can set their own
  theme volume without dashboard access. (Shipped broken - fixed in 1.0.2.)
- Adjusted copies are now encoded at the lower of the source bitrate and a per-codec ceiling
  rather than always around 190 kbps, so a 128 kbps theme is no longer inflated.
- The encoder settings are part of the cache key, so changing them invalidates the cache by
  itself.
- Fixed the config page status panel printing the same sentence twice.
- Initial release.
